Abstract: Abstract This chapter discusses the main findings of the book and the implications for theory and method, and the empirical applications of the mixture model. It recaps the idea that according to the mixture model, policy change is generated by mixtures of many contributions which vary over time and across issue areas. It highlights two results: country-level factors such as institutional arrangements and degrees of democracy are associated with the shapes of spending change distributions, and similar issues do not have similar distributions across countries. It also stresses the importance of data treatment, and how pooling and aggregation affect distributions. Title: Legal Model for Post-Flood Ecological Disaster Recovery in North Sumatra, Indonesia
Abstract: This paper examines how corruption and environmental crimes committed by PT Toba Pulp Lestari have produced flash floods, ecological disasters, and the extinction of villages in Tapanuli, North Sumatra. Drawing on normative juridical analysis and case study of legal documents, court decisions, and civil society reports, it traces three mechanisms of corporate-state crime: financial corruption through transfer pricing and asset depreciation, environmental crimes through deforestation of 67,000 hectares of customary forest, and criminalization of Indigenous land defenders under the Job Creation Law. The article shows how law has been instrumentalized against Indigenous claims, creating what Nancy Fraser terms ‘abnormal justice’. In response, it proposes a legal action model comprising revocation of TPL’s concession through administrative courts, actio popularis for ecosystem recovery, and ratification of the Indigenous Peoples Bill. The analysis contributes a socio-legal framework for contesting corporate-state crime in Indonesia.
Authors: Marulak Pardede

Title: Value Transformations of Modern Russian Constitutionalism and Their Influence on the Constitutional Law Model of Direct Grassroots Democracy
Abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of value and ideological transformations affecting the constitutional and legal model of direct democracy in modern Russia. The author explores the departure from liberal individualistic principles in favor of the concept of a moral state based on spiritual unity, the priority of public interests and cultural and historical continuity. Special attention is paid to rethinking the role of local self-government, which is considered not as an element of the mechanics of power, but as a form of self-organization of local communities. The paper substantiates the thesis about the insufficiency and crisis of traditional direct forms of expression of will (elections, referendums) and raises the question of the need to recognize alternative, corporate and conciliar practices of identifying the will of the people as full-fledged institutions of democracy. The author concludes that constitutional reform and doctrinal re-traditionalization consolidate a consolidated understanding of national unity, calling into question the monopoly of the party system on political representation.
Authors: Sergey S. Zenin
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06

Title: Meningkatkan Keterampilan Berpikir Kritis, Pemecahan Masalah Dan Kolaborasi Matematika Menggunakan Model RAKAT Pada Siswa SD
Abstract: Rendahnya keterampilan berpikir kritis, pemecahan masalah, kolaborasi, dan hasil belajar siswa kelas V SDN 1 Komet Banjarbaru dipengaruhi oleh pembelajaran yang masih berpusat pada guru dan kurang kontekstual. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan aktivitas guru dan siswa serta menganalisis peningkatan keterampilan berpikir kritis, pemecahan masalah, kolaborasi, dan hasil belajar melalui penerapan Model RAKAT yang mengintegrasikan Problem Based Learning (PBL), Realistic Mathematics Education (RME), dan Numbered Heads Together (NHT). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan dengan data kualitatif dan kuantitatif dalam jenis Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilaksanakan dalam tiga pertemuan pada 28 siswa kelas V. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, tes, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif kualitatif dan kuantitatif. Title: Consensus-Based Pricing Model for Professional Services: A Legal and Technological Approach in Indonesia
Abstract: The digital economy has significantly expanded professional service transactions in Indonesia; however, no established mechanism currently provides a reliable benchmark for determining fair service fees. This gap has contributed to price disparities, information asymmetry, and unequal bargaining power between service providers and clients. This study aims to examine the legal framework governing professional service pricing, assess the compatibility of a consensus-based pricing model with competition law principles, and develop a conceptual Consensus-Based Pricing Model. The study employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches. The findings demonstrate that the proposed model does not constitute price fixing, as it merely provides a transparent, non-binding, and informative pricing benchmark while preserving the parties' freedom to negotiate the final price. By leveraging digital platforms through a co-regulatory approach, the model has the potential to reduce information asymmetry, strengthen consumer protection and legal certainty, and promote fair market competition.
Authors: Nanin Koeswidi Astuti
Categories: Uncategorized
Published: 2026-08-06
